name: ADA University
summary: Predominantly English degrees in Baku; compulsory Azerbaijani-taught core courses need checking before non-speakers apply.

ib.text: International applicants submit school records and attend an English interview if shortlisted. The 25-point IB route is for Azerbaijani applicants; confirm international IB rules and Azerbaijani-course provision.

notes: The published Foundation Program normally includes two Azerbaijani-taught core courses; no exemption for international non-speakers was established.
Fall 2027 dates, fees and programme availability are not confirmed; 2026 domestic IB deadlines and the 2025 fee table are not current international terms.
The largely bilingual Law degree is excluded; international applicants use ADA and Study in Azerbaijan applications, separate from the Azerbaijani-citizen route.

programmes.name: International Studies
programmes.about: An interdisciplinary degree examining international affairs, world cultures, government and global challenges, culminating in an applied capstone.
programmes.overview: Students investigate international politics, social change, cultures and the economic forces shaping cross-border issues. The degree combines perspectives from several disciplines with research, analysis and communication skills. Near graduation, a capstone project applies what students have learned to a practical situation. The programme describes routes into public institutions, diplomacy, business, education and further study.
programmes.ib: Predominantly English; the foundation normally requires two Azerbaijani-taught courses. Confirm provision for non-speakers and 2027 IB requirements before applying.
programmes.selectionNote: International route: academic records reviewed, then an English interview for shortlisted applicants. Programme-specific 2027 tests or portfolios are not confirmed.

programmes.name: Communication and Digital Media
programmes.about: A communication and media degree integrating communication theory, digital content production, writing and audience-focused information work.
programmes.overview: Students examine communication theory alongside digital-media practice, writing, presenting and producing content for different audiences. The curriculum includes research, media-related courses and upper-level electives that allow students to deepen a particular interest. Coursework develops the ability to communicate through different formats and manage information in professional settings. Graduates may pursue communication and media work or continue their studies.

programmes.name: Public Affairs
programmes.about: An undergraduate public-policy degree combining quantitative analysis, public administration, communication and applied problem-solving.
programmes.overview: Students learn to analyse policy problems, assess evidence and consider how public decisions affect communities and institutions. The programme develops quantitative reasoning, communication and understanding of governance and public affairs. Elective choices provide scope to explore other fields, while a capstone project requires application to a real-world issue. Its stated destinations span public agencies, nonprofit organisations and the private sector.

programmes.name: Business Administration
programmes.about: A broad business degree covering management, accounting, finance, marketing, operations and organisational decision-making.
programmes.overview: Students build a common foundation in economics, accounting, management and quantitative business methods. Subsequent courses explore marketing, finance, organisational behaviour, strategy and the operation of businesses. The curriculum combines analytical study with project-based work, electives and opportunities to apply business concepts to practical problems. It is designed for employment across business functions or further study in management-related fields.

programmes.name: Economics
programmes.about: A quantitative economics degree focused on markets, policy, microeconomics, macroeconomics and statistical evidence.
programmes.overview: Students study how households, firms and governments make decisions and how markets and national economies function. The course develops mathematical and statistical analysis through microeconomics, macroeconomics, econometrics and related methods. Upper-level modules address applied economic questions, with research and analytical work supporting evidence-based interpretation. The degree supports progression to economics-oriented roles in public or private organisations and postgraduate study.

programmes.name: Finance
programmes.about: A finance degree examining financial institutions, investment, valuation, corporate finance and the quantitative analysis of risk.
programmes.overview: Students combine finance with economics, accounting, mathematics and statistics to understand financial choices and institutions. The curriculum covers corporate finance, investment analysis, valuation, financial markets and management of financial risk. Applied coursework and a capstone connect theoretical models with financial decision-making. Graduates can pursue finance-related roles in firms and financial institutions or advanced study.

programmes.name: Computer Science
programmes.about: A computing degree built around programming, algorithms, software systems, operating systems and applied problem-solving.
programmes.overview: Students study programming and the conceptual foundations of computing, including algorithms, data structures and computer systems. Courses address software development, operating systems and related technical topics, with electives offering more specialised study. The programme emphasises practical tasks, problem-solving and collaborative work in addition to theory. Graduates are prepared for software and computing roles and may continue to specialist postgraduate study.

programmes.name: Computer Engineering
programmes.about: An engineering degree integrating computer hardware, embedded electronics, networks and the software that controls computing devices.
programmes.overview: Students learn how electronic hardware and software interact, building foundations in programming, mathematics and engineering. Major courses cover circuits, digital systems, computer architecture, networks and embedded devices. Laboratories and design-based coursework provide practical opportunities to connect component-level understanding with working systems. The degree leads toward computer engineering and systems-related work or further technical study.

programmes.name: Information Technology
programmes.about: An applied IT degree concerned with software applications, information systems, networks and the organisational use of technology.
programmes.overview: Students learn to build and maintain digital systems for organisations, combining technical computing skills with understanding of user needs. The course includes programming, databases, networking and information-systems analysis, with applied work on software and services. Further study in areas such as security, web development and IT management supports different technical pathways. The programme is oriented toward practical technology roles and continued professional learning.

programmes.name: Mathematics
programmes.about: A mathematics degree developing proof, abstract reasoning and quantitative methods across pure and applied mathematics.
programmes.overview: Students build rigorous skills in calculus, algebra and mathematical reasoning, then progress to more advanced mathematical structures and methods. The course catalogue includes analysis, probability, statistics and differential equations alongside computational or applied topics. Mathematical problem-solving and proof are central to the degree, with electives supporting individual interests. Graduates may pursue quantitative work or further academic study in mathematics and adjacent disciplines.

programmes.name: Electrical and Electronics Engineering
programmes.about: A dual-degree engineering programme covering electronic circuits, control, communications and embedded systems, including study in Italy.
programmes.overview: Students develop foundations in physics, mathematics, electric circuits, electronics and digital systems. Laboratories and engineering design work connect theory with applications such as communications, networks and embedded control. ADA states that the programme is offered jointly with Politecnico di Torino and includes one semester of study in Italy. Successful students are described as earning bachelor degrees from both institutions, subject to the dual-degree requirements.

programmes.name: Agricultural Technologies
programmes.about: An agronomy degree on crop production, plant health, soil and water management, farm technologies and sustainable agriculture.
programmes.overview: Students study crop and tree production, agricultural ecosystems, soil chemistry, plant protection and farm machinery. Practical components include laboratories, experimental fields and greenhouses, as well as a required professional internship. The programme also teaches agricultural water management and the economic and environmental dimensions of production. It prepares students for technical roles across farms, agricultural businesses, public bodies and further study in agronomy-related fields.

programmes.name: Food Technologies
programmes.about: A food-science degree exploring processing, food chemistry, microbiology, safety and product quality in food production systems.
programmes.overview: Students study the scientific basis of food processing and preservation, including food chemistry, microbiology and quality assessment. The curriculum combines technical subjects with food-production systems and the assessment of product safety and characteristics. Laboratories and practical experience link scientific concepts to industrial or research problems. Graduates can pursue work in food production, food-quality activities or further specialised study.

programmes.name: Animal Science
programmes.about: An animal-production degree addressing husbandry, genetics, nutrition, health, welfare and modern livestock management.
programmes.overview: Students study animal nutrition, genetics, reproduction, comparative pathology and the management of livestock production. The programme includes animal-health and food-hygiene topics and introduces precision methods used in modern husbandry. Practical learning takes place through laboratories, experimental farms and a professional internship with a company or research laboratory. It prepares students for technical and management roles in animal production and related further study.

programmes.name: Architecture
programmes.about: A design-led architecture degree spanning buildings, interiors, urban context, heritage, technical methods and environmental considerations.
programmes.overview: Students explore architecture through design, history, theory, technical knowledge and the relationship between buildings and their settings. Work spans interior, architectural and urban or landscape scales, with studio-based projects connecting analysis to design decisions. The curriculum considers construction methods, cultural heritage and environmental responsibilities. The degree develops the foundation for architectural practice-related work and advanced architectural education, subject to local professional rules.

programmes.name: Interior Design
programmes.about: A spatial-design degree on interior environments, materials, furniture, human use, representation and design technology.
programmes.overview: Students investigate how interior spaces function and how design choices shape users’ experiences. Studio assignments combine spatial composition, drawing and digital representation with study of materials, lighting and the existing built environment. Technical and historical subjects support the development of coherent design proposals and communication of ideas. The course prepares students for interior-design work and further study in design-related fields.

programmes.name: Urban Planning
programmes.about: An urban and regional planning degree integrating spatial analysis, city design, sustainability, landscape and planning policy.
programmes.overview: Students examine how cities, regions and landscapes change and how planning decisions affect communities and space. Coursework joins planning theory with mapping, geographic information systems, sustainability and public-policy context. A sequence of studios develops practical skills in analysing places and designing proposals at urban and regional scales. The programme describes opportunities in public institutions, planning studios, research and specialised postgraduate study.

programmes.name: Communication Design
programmes.about: A visual communication degree combining analogue and digital design, typography, media, information and design research.
programmes.overview: Students learn to shape visual information and communication experiences for different media and audiences. Practical studios introduce design methods, drawing, typography, digital media and the production of communication artefacts. Historical and critical study helps students evaluate the social context and clarity of designed messages. The programme prepares graduates for communication-design work in companies, institutions or studios, or postgraduate study.
